# Code of conduct

## Our pledge

We want our community to be welcoming, safe, and fair for everyone.

We respect the dignity, rights, and contributions of every person, whatever
their:

- race, ethnicity, caste, or color
- age or physical characteristics
- neurodiversity or disability
- sex or gender, gender identity or expression, or sexual orientation
- language, philosophy, or religion
- national or social origin, socio-economic position, or level of education
- other status

Everyone who takes part in good faith and follows this code has the same rights
to take part.

## Expected behavior

Social norms differ between people. Your words and actions can also read
differently from what you intend, because of culture, background, or native
language. Keep this in mind and act with care toward each other.

In this community, we:

1. Respect the purpose of the community, its activities, and the ways we meet.
2. Talk to others kindly and honestly.
3. Respect viewpoints and experiences that differ from our own.
4. Take responsibility for our actions and contributions.
5. Give and accept constructive feedback with grace.
6. Repair harm when we cause it.
7. Act in other ways that keep the community healthy.

## Restricted behavior

The behaviors in the two lists below are not permitted. Doing them, threatening
to do them, or encouraging them violates this code.

1. Harassment: crossing a boundary that a person states clearly, or giving a
   person attention they do not want after they ask you to stop.
2. Character attacks: insulting or demeaning comments about a community member
   or a group of people.
3. Stereotyping or discrimination: judging the personality or behavior of a
   person from an identity or trait they cannot change.
4. Sexualization: behavior that most people would find too intimate for the
   community and its purpose.
5. Violating confidentiality: sharing or using the personal or private
   information of a person without their permission.
6. Endangerment: causing, encouraging, or threatening violence or other harm
   to any person or group.
7. Other behavior that threatens the health of the community.

### Other restrictions

1. Misleading identity: pretending to be another person for any reason,
   including to avoid enforcement.
2. Missing credit: contributing content without crediting its sources.
3. Promotion: sharing marketing or other commercial content in a way that
   goes against the norms of the community.
4. Irresponsible communication: presenting content that includes, links to, or
   describes restricted behavior without care.

## Report a violation

Conflicts can happen even when everyone tries their best. Not every conflict
violates this code. The expected behavior above helps to prevent conflicts and
to reduce harm.

If a violation occurs, report it quickly. Use the
[private report form](https://github.com/sravioli/lantern.wz/security/advisories/new)
of this repository. Only the maintainer,
[@sravioli](https://github.com/sravioli), can read these reports. Do not report
violations in public issues or pull requests. To report content on GitHub
itself, you can also use
[Report abuse](https://docs.github.com/en/communities/maintaining-your-safety-on-github/reporting-abuse-or-spam)
on GitHub.

The maintainer takes every report seriously and tries to reply quickly. To
investigate a report, the maintainer can read messages, logs, and recordings,
and can talk to witnesses and other participants.

The maintainer keeps the investigation as open as possible, but safety and
privacy come first. For this reason, the maintainer handles enforcement in
private with the people involved. The people involved can agree to share the
outcome with the whole community.

## Repair harm

If an investigation finds a violation, the maintainer can use the steps below
to decide how to repair the harm. The decision depends on how the incident
affected the people involved and the community. For a serious violation, the
maintainer can skip the lower steps.

1. Warning
   1. Event: one violation, or a series of violations.
   2. Consequence: a private, written warning from the maintainer.
   3. Repair: for example, a private written apology, accepting
      responsibility, or asking what the community expects.
2. Temporary limits
   1. Event: a violation that happens again after a warning, or a first
      violation that is more serious.
   2. Consequence: a private, written warning and a cooldown period with an
      end date. The cooldown shows how serious the situation is and gives
      the people involved time to think about the incident. It can apply only
      to some communication channels or to contact with some members.
   3. Repair: for example, an apology, time to think about the actions and
      their effect, and care when returning after the cooldown ends.
3. Temporary suspension
   1. Event: a pattern of violations that warnings did not stop, or one
      serious violation.
   2. Consequence: a private, written warning that states the conditions for
      return. A suspension gives the suspended person time to think about
      their behavior and how to change it.
   3. Repair: for example, respecting the purpose of the suspension, meeting
      the conditions for return, and care when joining the community again.
4. Permanent ban
   1. Event: a pattern of violations that the other steps did not stop. It can
      also be a violation so serious that the maintainer cannot keep the
      community safe with this person in it.
   2. Consequence: the person loses access to all community spaces, tools,
      and communication channels. The maintainer uses a ban rarely, only with
      a strong reason, and only when other remedies did not change the
      behavior.
   3. Repair: none is possible at this level.

These steps are a guide. They do not limit the judgment of the maintainer, who
acts in the interest of the community.

## Scope

This code applies in all community spaces. It also applies when a person
officially represents the community in public or in other spaces. A person
represents the community when they:

- use an official email address
- post from an official social media account
- act as an appointed representative at an online or offline event
